name: Integration test
meaning: A test compiled as an external consumer of a library’s public interface.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Domain error
meaning: A typed failure representing a violated application rule, with intentionally chosen context.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Box ownership
meaning: Unique ownership of a heap allocation through an owning pointer with a finite-sized representation.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Reference-counted ownership
meaning: Keeping an allocation alive while one or more strong owning pointers refer to it.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Runtime borrow guard
meaning: A value whose lifetime represents a currently active RefCell borrow.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Atomic shared ownership
meaning: Reference-counted ownership with thread-safe count updates, subject to the payload’s thread-safety bounds.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Mutex guard
meaning: An owned lock token that provides protected access and releases the lock when dropped.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Join handle
meaning: A handle used to wait for a thread and observe its returned value or panic.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Sender lifetime
meaning: The period during which sender handles can still produce messages; receiver iteration ends only after all senders are gone and queued values drained.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Send and Sync
meaning: Marker traits for safe transfer of ownership and safe sharing of references across threads, respectively.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Atomic read-modify-write
meaning: An indivisible operation that reads an atomic value, computes a change and stores it.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Error propagation
meaning: Returning a failure to the caller rather than silently substituting a successful-looking value.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Bounded line parsing
meaning: Reading and validating lines under explicit input-size, line-count and value limits.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Path value
meaning: A platform-aware representation of a filesystem location, not proof that the location exists.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Argument validation
meaning: Checking the number and meaning of command-line values before relying on them.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Validation policy
meaning: The explicitly chosen normalization, syntax and domain rules determining which inputs are accepted.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Display contract
meaning: User-facing formatting through a borrowed Formatter with a returned formatting Result.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Lazy future
meaning: A value describing asynchronous work whose body does not progress until driven by polling.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Bounded future poll
meaning: A deliberately limited poll of a known-ready future, not a runtime for arbitrary asynchronous work.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Macro evaluation count
meaning: The number of times an expanded macro causes a captured expression to execute.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Unsafe contract
meaning: A safety obligation that must be upheld for an operation requiring unsafe, not a waiver of Rust’s validity rules.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Bounded validation pipeline
meaning: A finite sequence of parsing, domain filtering and capped collection with an explicit rejection policy.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.
